Released at 2026-10-19

* FEATURE: **The existing lint findings of the parity and chaos test helpers are cleared (tests only, no behaviour change).** Seven findings in `tests/parity` and `tests/e2e` (unchecked `Body.Close` and `json.Unmarshal` results, a redundant nil check, and the complexity of `TestParity_CrossValidation`, whose two sum-per-label subtests now share one helper) no longer fail the lint step's only-new-issues pass on a very large PR, which treats every existing finding of a package as new when it cannot fetch the PR's patch.
* FEATURE: **A tombstone only turns the metadata fast paths off for the files it can match, and a file that must be read is matched per block (both binaries).** A tombstone used to switch off, for every file of the window, the manifest-answered counts, the label-count push-down, the metadata-only row-group reads and the field-value aggregates, and to add its fields to every read; every row of every read file was then matched against every overlapping tombstone through a fresh map, so the cost grew with the number of tombstones. Now a file is read as if there were no tombstone when its own metadata proves, from memory only (no S3 read), that no tombstone acting on its tenant can match a row of it: its time range, a complete manifest label set, or the pmeta bloom for an exact `field:="v"` / `field:in(...)` term on a registered column. Anything undecided (regex, NOT, OR, empty value, prefix, map attribute, unknown bounds, no pmeta) keeps the old path, so every answer is unchanged. The label set of a compaction output is never used (recognised by its level or its `compacted-` key): compaction unions its inputs' sets, which is partial when an input had none ([#621](https://github.com/ReliablyObserve/victoria-lakehouse/issues/621)). In-process, 8 objects, upstream-shaped tombstones at K = 1, 10 and 100, against main (medians of 6 interleaved runs, every answer equal): with tombstones no file holds, `stats by (service.name) count()` 7.9, 16.4 and 109.7 ms become 5.1, 5.0 and 4.8 ms with 0 object reads instead of 8; with a map-attribute tombstone nothing is provable and the per-block matcher alone takes `field_names` from 21.7, 45.4 and 295.5 ms to 15.6, 16.8 and 24.0 ms; with no tombstone nothing moves. `count()` and hits are answered from the manifest only for a request that carries the timestamp-only hint, which no served handler sets today; the count push-down, the field-value aggregates and every scan do not need it. New section "Per-file gating of a delete" in `docs/read-path.md`.
